newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs seen moving sideways, waiting on CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs seen moving sideways, waiting on CVRD.

text.p: Brazilian stocks were seen opening directionless as players wait to see if the government can pull off the planned sale of state miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce despite a host of lawsuits, brokers said.
"The privatization of CVRD will set the tone for the day," said one local trader. "My feeling is, if it happens, it will be late in the day."
Sao Paulo's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares ended up 0.31 percent Monday at 9,762 points despite worries about suits piling up against the CVRD selloff.
Brokers said the CVRD auction, billed as the largest privatization in Latin American history, is expected to dominate trade through the day.
The selloff was set for 1000 local/0900 EDT on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange but most observors expect delays.
Some brokers said that, if the government manages to defuse the legal challenges quickly, the auction could take place later in the session while others expect it will be put off to another date.
"If the auction goes ahead ... it should certainly provide a morale boost to investors in Brazil which could help stengthen the market over the coming days," one analyst said.

Traders also said the session would be affected by release this week of key U.S. economic indicators as well as growing concern about the snail's pace of Brazil's fiscal, pension and civil service reforms.
"It's something I'm definitely worried about," one broker said. "The IMF has been sending warnings about this problem and its impact on external accounts."

Financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said Brazil's international reserves dropped $2.144 billion in April's first 25 days due to the payment of foreign debt interest and premiums and dollar sales in the floating forex market.
Meanwhile, power shares may be helped by news the government is considering a new electrical rate hike for the peak hour of 6 p.m. to 7 p.m. in Brazil's southeastern industrial heartland.
Telebras preferred up 0.21 pct at 120.50 reais.
